full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 12 dated 29-11-2021 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 2019 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, briefly, are that the present opposite party as applicant (herein after called as the opposite party) on 4-4-2019 filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 2019 under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka for appointment of the arbitrator on behalf of the petitioner as to settlement of the dispute between the parties in the arbitration proceedings pursuant to notice dated 13-2-2019 contending, inter-alia, that he is a 25% share holder of Southbay Properties Ltd. House No. 53, Road No. 15, Sector No. 11, Uttara Model Town, Dhaka by investing Taka 71 Lac although the applicant-opposite party, AKM Shahidul Alam is not getting any profit from the said company and hence, the opposite party wants to appoint an arbitrators for solution of the dispute between the parties as per article 29 of the Articles of Association of the said company. 

 8. In this background all on a sudden Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Senior Advocate died and thereafter, the opposite party filed an application dated 10-11-2021 in the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 2019 submitting the name of Mr Mintu Kumar Mandol, the learned Advocate, Supreme Court of Bangladesh as his arbitrator in place of deceased Mr Abdul Matin Khashru before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. 

 10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order No. 12 dated 29-11-2021 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 2019 the petitioner, Shahidur Rahman Chowdhury moved before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 11. Mr Motahar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner at the very outset takes me through the order sheets of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 2019 and thereafter, points out that the miscellaneous case was disposed of by Order No. 10 dated 1-8-2019 by the learned District Judge although the learned District Judge, Dhaka without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject most illegally reopened the miscellaneous case and allowed the prayer of the opposite party for appointment of their arbitrator, which resulted in the failure of justice. The learned Advocate further points out that Order No. 12 dated 29-11-2021 passed by the learned District Judge is not a proper order in the eye of law inasmuch as the learned District Judge by order No. 10 dated 1-8-2019 has already been disposed of the arbitration miscellaneous case and therefore, the learned District Judge being functus officio cannot reopen the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act and or pass any order therein and, as such, the learned District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice.
